media_bytes.description: Size of the published media file, as fetched on accessed_at.

media_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the published media file. A fetch that reproduces this digest reproduces the excerpt; see scripts/fetch_benchmark_media.py.

content_fingerprint.description: How to establish that another copy is this recording, when bytes cannot: a source that re-encodes gives every downloader a different file, so a digest pins nothing. The fingerprint describes the sound instead, and survives re-encoding. Verified truth needs one of the two, because an anchor into bytes nobody can confirm is not evidence.

method.description: Identifies the procedure and its version, so a reader knows which tool reads this file.

path.description: Repository path of the committed fingerprint, relative to the repository root. Constrained here as well as in the validator: a manifest is data, and a path with a leading slash or a .. segment would send whatever reads it outside the repository, which both reads what it should not and voids the point of the field - that the fingerprint is committed where a reader can already see it.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the fingerprint file itself. This one does pin bytes: the fingerprint is committed here, so it cannot be re-encoded underneath a reader.

capture_layout.description: How the speakers were captured, stated only as far as the recording establishes it. single_mixed_track says what a mixdown measurably is - one track, no per-speaker channel to diarize from - and deliberately claims nothing about where the speakers were, since room topology is rarely measurable from a published file. Where the speakers actually were belongs in observations, with its evidence, rather than in an enum a consumer will read alone.

expected_physical_speakers.description: The upper reading of how many people speak: distinct speaking roles heard, before allowing for one person covering two of them. Read it with proven_distinct_speakers, which is the floor; the true count lies between.

proven_distinct_speakers.description: How many speakers are demonstrably different people, by evidence stated in observations. Never larger than expected_physical_speakers. Proving k distinct people needs k speakers established as pairwise distinct from one another: counting the speakers named across a list of pairwise observations overstates it, because a chain of pairs can be satisfied by two people. A diarization score should be read against this floor as well as the estimate.

music_or_effects.description: Whether music or effects appear in the recording. null means the question was not answered, which covers both cases the corpus uses it for: a candidate ruled out on rights before anyone listened, and a recording assessed only by sampling. false claims an end-to-end inspection, so use it only when one was done.

annotation_status.description: How far this item's own truth layer has got. verified means every target met the bar the corpus sets for verification - anchored, with evidence, from an observation of the recording - and it deliberately does not distinguish a human ear from tooling, because that distinction lives per target in basis and per item in truth.method. Read alone this enum therefore reads stronger than some items' evidence: an item can be verified with no audio_observed target anywhere in it. Anything deciding what a score means has to read truth.method, and anything reporting one has to say which.

threads.description: Subjects that open early and are still live late, recorded as the distance between the first and last anchor that carries them. This is the property a short excerpt cannot exhibit at all, and the reason a multi-hour item exists: a system can capture every entity in a four-hour session and still fail to notice that the thing settled in the last ten minutes is the thing raised in the first ten. Each end must be the anchor of a truth target, so a thread cannot be asserted without the observations that hold it up.

method.description: How the truth was established, including which provider produced any machine-assisted output. Required once any target is verified, so a score is never read without its annotation provenance.

contaminating_providers.description: Providers that helped build this truth and therefore cannot be scored against it without declaring the dependency. Machine-readable so a scoring run can refuse the combination instead of relying on someone having read the notes. Required once any target is machine-assisted.

negative_controls.description: Terms an annotator established are absent from the excerpt, so that a run asserting one is drawing on metadata, on a title, or on prior sessions rather than on the audio it was given. This is the one thing in an answer key that can be checked without judging whether two sentences mean the same thing, which makes it the strongest single measurement the corpus supports - and it only works if the annotator established absence rather than merely failing to notice the term. Structured rather than described in truth.notes because a scoring run has to act on it.

license_url.description: URL of the license document, or null when the source is all-rights-reserved and no license document exists.

term.description: The term itself, spelled as a system would plausibly produce it. Matched as whole words, so a control of one common word is a control that fires on noise.

kind.description: Where a system would have got the term from if it produced one. This is what makes a hit diagnostic rather than merely wrong: title_metadata says the episode title supplies it, later_in_episode says the recording contains it outside the annotated window, prior_session says it belongs to the campaign but not this excerpt.

rationale.description: How absence was established, and over what span. Absence is a stronger claim than presence and is easier to get wrong: 'no decode of this window produced it' is evidence, 'I did not notice it' is not. State which.

first_anchor_ms.description: Where the thread opens. Must be the anchor_ms of a truth target in this manifest.

last_anchor_ms.description: Where the thread is last carried. Must be the anchor_ms of a truth target in this manifest, and later than first_anchor_ms.

evidence.description: What is observable at each end and what makes them the same thread. A pair of anchors that merely mention a word is a word frequency, not a thread; what is claimed here is that the later moment is about the earlier one.

kind.description: person is a physical speaker at the table; character is the fiction they voice. The two are deliberately separate kinds.

anchor_ms.description: Where the target is observable, in milliseconds on the same basis as the excerpt window. Must fall inside that window.

basis.description: How the target was found, named for the strongest evidence behind it. audio_observed means a person listened to the recording and heard it - this is the human-ear value, and nothing weaker may use it. audio_machine_assisted means the recording was read through tooling, which is verifiable but carries a dependency on whatever produced the reading. metadata_inferred came from a title, description, or index, and cannot be scored as capability. Only the first two can be verified. A target first read by tooling and later confirmed by ear becomes audio_observed, and its evidence says both things happened, because one field cannot carry a history. A spelling settled from a written source is not an ear observation: the audio establishes the word, the source establishes how it is written, and the evidence has to say which did which.
